title: High-Resolution Characterization of Ceramic Nanorods and Their Surfaces to Optimize Ion Transport in Composite Polymer/Ceramic Electrolytes
content: In the drive to improve safety and decrease flammability of consumer battery devices, the attention of the research community has turned to polymer electrolytes [1]. However, while providing a substantial safety boost, polymer electrolytes such as poly(ethylene oxide)-Li salt have lower ionic mobility compared to their liquid analogues. One of the emerging strategies to improve polymer ionic conductivity has become the incorporation of highly ionically conductive ceramic particles into the polymer, creating a composite electrolyte [2]. After some encouraging reports of the significant improvements in ionic conductivity using this approach, a more nuanced picture has emerged: in some cases, the increase in the conductivity – or whether it increases at all – can be changed by changing the morphology of the ceramic nanoparticles, such as when particle aspect ratio changes from ∼1 for conventional powder to >>1 for nanorods [3].
